verdict: A well-instrumented, honest engineering notebook with a genuinely good small core (history-based references with declared cardinality, interaction-derived ΔH/ΔS/volume contracts, edit-stability harness) wrapped in an architecture that largely re-derives semantic feature modelling, KBE, SE requirement allocation and design rationale without engaging them. No model, intent checks or solver exist yet. Biggest risks: false assurance (PASS on a demo that likely fails its load intent), interpretations letting checks select geometry, and a workflow that presumes designers know and will state intent. Ship the verifier/benchmark first.

items.title: Intent tree + check flow-down is not new
items.claim: Pass/allocate/translate/derive is systems-engineering requirement allocation; intent→checks→solution mirrors Gero's FBS; 'tree is the rationale' is the IBIS/gIBIS/QOC/DRed promise. None cited.
items.remedy: Add a prior-art section stating the delta: executable rationale bound to geometry, and why it beats the known failure modes.

items.title: Rule packs and idiomatic score have commercial precedent
items.claim: KBE (ICAD, NX Knowledge Fusion, CATIA Knowledgeware, Creo Behavioral Modeling), DFM/DFA checkers and model-quality checkers (Q-Checker, CADIQ, VDA 4955, SASIG PDQ) already do this; KBE's lesson is rule-base maintenance cost.
items.remedy: Position packs against KBE; budget pack maintenance.

items.title: Closest prior art (semantic feature modelling) missing
items.claim: Bidarra & Bronsvoort 2000 attach validity constraints to features checked after each edit; Shah & Mäntylä 1995; valid-parameter-range work (Hoffmann & Kim 2001; Joan-Arinyo); CAD-education design-intent rubrics (Company, Contero, Camba, Otey). 'Nobody measures intent' holds only for the ML literature.
items.evidence: reports/Parametric CAD generation survey.md 'Benchmarks measure shape similarity'; docs/explore-further.md
items.remedy: Read and cite; narrow novelty claims.

items.title: Genuinely new parts are smaller and concrete
items.claim: Interpretations with elimination and sensitivity-gated questions (nearest analogue: PBE disambiguation, Mayer et al. 2015); interaction-derived per-feature ΔH/ΔS/volume contracts; an edit-stability benchmark over an open DSL.
items.remedy: Lead with these; publish the benchmark.
items.uncertainty: medium: there may be unpublished industrial equivalents

items.title: First adopters are not early-stage industrial designers
items.claim: Best fits: parametric families/configurators, CadQuery/build123d makers, and AI agents via MCP as a verifier. Early ID (sketches, images) is the weakest fit.
items.remedy: Say so in the README; design v1 around the agent-verifier use case.

items.title: 'All non-determinism on the intent side' is false in the engine
items.claim: Build depends on lock/prefs/reading tables; no-lock builds use unchecked defaults; Gauss–Seidel with warm start is path-dependent; server re-resolves in the background and rebuilds ~2.5 s later; BRepOffset bytes nondeterministic; the DSL is arbitrary Python with cached imports.
items.remedy: Define determinism over a fully locked solution; make the lock mandatory for displayed/exported builds; fail closed.

items.title: 'Literals only for true design parameters' contradicted by the example
items.claim: 0.75, 0.8, 6, 0.4, shelf_hole_u=0.75, plain(8.0), across=0.5, TOOL_ACCESS_DIAMETER=30 in the example; engine epsilons 1 mm, +2 mm, 0.01 mm, 16 rays. Multiplying by a parameter is not a relation.
items.remedy: Classify relation / ratio constant / engine epsilon and count separately in the metric.

items.title: The example has the false coupling the architecture warns against
items.claim: width = 6*t (thickness 5→8 widens the bracket 30→48 mm); leg and gusset scale with shelf_depth without stated purpose; §8.6 edit tests pass because of these couplings.
items.remedy: Make independent parameters or justify each ratio with an intent node and check.

items.title: Interpretations turn checks into selection pressure
items.claim: Invariants eliminate readings and then report PASS on the survivor. The spike-01 negative control (shelf_hole_u=0.4) now silently drills through_all into the gusset with only a non-blocking notice; rule #32 was narrowed until the demo showed 0 notices.
items.evidence: src/dipm/interpret.py steps 2 and 6; NOTES DECISIONS #28, #32; docs/architecture.md §10 item 2
items.remedy: Ask (not notify) on extra interaction; keep hold-out checks never used for elimination; show 'selected' distinct from 'verified'.

items.title: A check compiled into a construction can never fail
items.claim: R.c4 tool access is a check in the docs but implemented as a placement (before(gusset, clearance=tool_access_radius)); nothing verifies it independently.
items.remedy: Keep checks as first-class objects that redundantly verify even relation-enforced intents (TODO 4).

items.title: Final bracket layout likely fails its own root load check; chosen for brevity
items.claim: Option 2 was chosen 'for brevity' although idiom passes should follow correctness. Screws at z≈9 and 50 mm on a 150 mm leg: M≈196 N×0.16 m≈31 N·m, T=M·z1/Σz²≈600 N on the upper anchor (≈1.2 kN with SF 2), vs ≈220 N with screws near the top.
items.remedy: Implement R.c1 as a hand-calc, show option 2 failing upward verification, let option 1 win.
items.uncertainty: medium: rigid-pivot model ignores wall bearing distribution and anchor stiffness; the ~2.7× ratio is robust

items.title: 'Proven' language outruns the report and code
items.claim: dsl §1 'provably complete alphabets', 'equivalence decided on the core', but there is no core IR (NOTES #4); the report says not to claim proven completeness until Mäntylä 1984 is read; dsl §5.5 'Laman exact in 2D' vs report §5.3 'generic only'.
items.evidence: docs/dsl.md §1, §5.5; NOTES DECISIONS #4; reports/DSL mathematical foundations.md §5.3, §7.5
items.remedy: Replace 'provably' with 'grounded in'; mark goals as goals.

items.title: 'Sensitivity none' conflates forced and insensitive
items.claim: A.3 reports 'none' because only one reading survived; arch claims 'same geometry everywhere in range' but only 9 sample points are checked.
items.remedy: Add 'forced: 1 survivor'; say 'identical at N sampled points'.

items.title: Topology-only hash described as invariant under legitimate edits
items.claim: Docstring says constant across legitimate edits, yet allow_topology_change exists because legitimate edits change topology.
items.remedy: Reword: a change is a review signal.

items.title: Stable dotted IDs vs hierarchy derived from dots
items.claim: Iteration 2 keeps IDs stable on move; connections.intent_tree derives hierarchy from the dots, so a reparented A.P.1 under B displays under A.
items.remedy: Opaque IDs plus explicit parent, or rewrite IDs on move.

items.title: Lock key ignores lowering code
items.claim: readings_digest hashes reading names/priors/complexity, not lowering implementations; changing what through_plate does leaves the lock fresh.
items.remedy: Include per-package version and a lowering-source hash.

items.title: Circular 'ground truth by construction' data claim
items.claim: Procedural trees give ground truth of the generator's ontology; a decomposer trained on them learns the generator's intents, not designers'.
items.remedy: State the limitation; build a small real-designer evaluation corpus from day one.

items.title: Euler–Poincaré check is a parity test
items.claim: H is solved from the formula; the check only fails on odd V−E+F−R or H<0. The diagnostic power is in ΔH vs an independent expectation.
items.remedy: Call it 'Euler parity'; compute H independently (Betti number via homology) if a real check is wanted.

items.title: Laman misapplied to CAD sketch constraints
items.claim: Laman/Pollaczek-Geiringer cover generic distance-only frameworks; CAD sketches mix angles, incidence, parallelism, tangency and are non-generic by design. Mixed direction-length frameworks need other counts (Servatius & Whiteley; Jackson & Jordán).
items.remedy: Structural counting as heuristic; numeric rank at a witness configuration (Michelucci & Foufou) as truth.

items.title: Ruler-and-compass core plus branch tags underspecified
items.claim: Many ordinary sketches are not decomposable/quadratic and fall to the numeric hatch; a deterministic seed gives repeatability, not continuity; a side predicate need not select a unique root.
items.remedy: Branch tags as orientation-determinant sign vectors; continuation along the parameter path; fail at discriminant crossings.

items.title: r-set closure doesn't buy manifold validity or coverage
items.claim: r-sets include non-manifold solids and the empty set; the proven core excludes fillet, countersink, draft and shell, which are most real features.
items.remedy: State r-set (not manifold) validity; add a manifoldness check; be explicit that real parts live in trusted primitives.

items.title: Cartan–Dieudonné/PGA have no operational role
items.claim: Transforms are lowered to reflections and re-emitted as native features; versor comparison needs sign canonicalisation and tolerance.
items.remedy: Footnote it; compare (R, t) with explicit tolerances.

items.title: Hashes are not canonical
items.claim: 4-round WL cannot separate many regular/symmetric graphs (common in CAD); docs call it canonical; 6-significant-figure rounding flips near boundaries across platforms.
items.remedy: WL as prefilter, nauty/bliss for equality, tolerance-aware geometric comparison.

items.title: No tolerance or robustness model
items.claim: Scattered, unstated epsilons (1 mm overshoot, +2 mm, 0.01 mm probe, 1e-9 volume) plus OCCT tolerances; no treatment of near-degenerate parameter regions; 9 samples miss thin invalid slivers.
items.remedy: One documented tolerance policy; near-coincidence linter; adaptive/interval sampling or computed validity intervals.

items.title: Differential geometry absent where ID aesthetics live
items.claim: Perception proxies ignore G1/G2/G3 continuity, curvature combs, highlight lines; OCCT rolling-ball fillets are G1; 'radius family ≤ 2' approves harsh tangent blends.
items.remedy: Add continuity and highlight-line proxies and curvature-continuous blend primitives.

items.title: Uncertainty labelled, not modelled
items.claim: Sensitivity is graded by volume % (blind to moved features at equal volume); no interval/probabilistic treatment of loads, PETG scatter, print tolerance; 'deterministic' rung 2 conflates repeatability with validity.
items.remedy: Interval/Monte Carlo propagation with margins; grade sensitivity by geometric distance.

items.title: Pinned learned scorer is not automatically deterministic
items.claim: GPU rendering/inference is not bit-reproducible by default.
items.remedy: Deterministic kernels/CPU, or a noise band on rung-3 scores.

items.title: Designers often don't know their intent yet
items.claim: Problem–solution co-evolution (Dorst & Cross), reflection-in-action (Schön); the root-intent-first flow forces premature commitment (Green's cognitive dimensions).
items.remedy: Geometry-first loose mode; intent optional per node; unexplained geometry is a legitimate draft state.

items.title: Design fixation and anchoring on defaults
items.claim: Ranked defaults and 'ask only when it matters' present one solution; exposure to one example fixates (Jansson & Smith 1991).
items.remedy: Show divergent alternatives side by side in exploratory phases.

items.title: Tacit knowledge doesn't encode cleanly
items.claim: 'Every gotcha becomes a permanent check' assumes articulable knowledge; mis-encoded rules over-constrain later designs.
items.remedy: Rules carry owner, scope, review date, and a one-click justified override.

items.title: Design-rationale tools died of maintenance cost
items.claim: IBIS/gIBIS/QOC failed on capture cost borne by non-beneficiaries (Grudin's asymmetry); iteration 2 adds .intent.yaml as a second source of truth.
items.remedy: Rationale as a by-product of existing actions (redlines, accepted proposals, answers); measure and display staleness.

items.title: Automation bias: green PASS on what doesn't matter
items.claim: The header and checks panel show PASS for developer invariants while none of R.c1–R.c4 runs.
items.remedy: Headline intent-check status ('0 of 4 intent checks implemented'); unverified = grey, never green.

items.title: Explanation overload and engine jargon
items.claim: Euler/ΔH/ΔS columns, 'sensitivity none', 'exposed_region_midpoint', 'A.P.holes.countersink(1)' are for kernel engineers.
items.remedy: Designer view: invariants only on failure, translated into physical language.

items.title: Intent-tree cognitive load at scale
items.claim: 9 intent nodes for 6 features; real products add feature tree, assembly tree, BOM; a third hierarchy will be ignored.
items.remedy: Intent as annotations on the feature tree; many-to-many links; test on a 150-feature part.

items.title: No handoff to engineering and manufacturing
items.claim: No datums, tolerances, GD&T, finish, drawings; 'geometry is not committed' collides with release/ECO culture; kernel upgrades could change released parts.
items.remedy: Release step freezing STEP + hash, rebuild diffs as ECOs; datum/tolerance intent before human packs.

items.title: Round-trip editing
items.claim: Hand edits in Onshape don't flow back; engineering will edit native CAD after handoff and the intent tree goes stale.
items.remedy: Bring the Onshape tab/FeatureScript path forward, or scope to cases where dipm stays source of truth.

items.title: Aesthetics beyond proxies; the Birkhoff lesson
items.claim: Birkhoff's Aesthetic Measure and golden-ratio rules failed because proxies reward order and penalise deliberate tension; named styles reduce culture to checklists; CMF absent.
items.remedy: Perception proxies as optional lint, never optimisation targets; designer (not crowd) preferences.

items.title: Learning curve and versioning culture
items.claim: Python/YAML/git workflow vs. industrial designers in Rhino/SolidWorks/KeyShot/paper.
items.remedy: Hide git behind save/compare/merge alternatives; Python as a power-user path.

items.title: System guesses harden into the designer's intent
items.claim: Model-made readings and assumptions are recorded under the designer's design; made_by is buried, so guessed and meant become indistinguishable.
items.remedy: Make model-made/unreviewed items visually distinct everywhere and let them expire to 'unknown'.

items.title: Geometry that changes on its own
items.claim: The server displays old-lock geometry then rebuilds ~2.5 s later with new interpretations.
items.remedy: Show 're-resolving…' and require a click when the result differs.

items.title: PASS badge with no intent checks; demo likely fails its load intent
items.claim: False assurance and automation bias.
items.evidence: GUI header; NOTES TODO 4; docs/architecture.md §8.1 R.c1; see INC-06, PAIN-05
items.remedy: Status line reports intent checks; implement R.c1 as a hand-calc first.

items.title: Interpretations use invariants to select geometry
items.claim: Negative controls become silent fixes; checks lose independence.
items.remedy: Ask on extra interaction; hold-out checks; 'selected' ≠ 'verified'.

items.title: Determinism claim leaks
items.claim: Central guarantee is weaker than stated (lock, prefs, warm start, background re-resolve, BRepOffset).
items.remedy: Define 'fully locked solution'; fail closed without a lock.

items.title: No model; learned skills without data; circular data argument
items.claim: Headline overclaims; the hardest part is untested.
items.remedy: Reframe v1 as an agent verifier; real-designer eval set.

items.title: Core prior art missing
items.claim: Reinvention and missed known failure modes.
items.remedy: Prior-art section; narrow novelty claims.

items.title: Handoff and round trip
items.claim: No tolerances/datums, geometry uncommitted, one-way export: blocks team use.
items.remedy: Release/freeze step; datum and tolerance intent; Onshape path sooner.

items.title: Laman 'exact in 2D'; no tolerance/robustness model
items.claim: Constraint-health and stability verdicts may be wrong.
items.evidence: docs/dsl.md §5.5; scattered epsilons; see MATH-02, MATH-07
items.remedy: Witness-rank checks; one tolerance policy; adaptive sampling.

items.title: Assumes known, stateable intent; fixation on defaults
items.claim: Misfit with early-stage industrial design.
items.remedy: Geometry-first loose mode; show alternatives.

items.title: Literals and convenience couplings in the canonical example
items.claim: Undermines principle 1 in its own showcase.
items.remedy: Separate params; classify ratios; fix the metric.

items.title: Hashes called canonical; Euler parity; ambiguous 'sensitivity none'
items.claim: Misleading signals where exactness is promised.
items.evidence: src/dipm/invariants.py; NOTES #25; see MATH-01, MATH-06, INC-08
items.remedy: Rename; nauty for equality; add a 'forced' state.

items.title: Reference layer: creator/role/source, declared cardinality, no ordinals, IsDeleted distrust, split/merge policies
items.claim: Reference layer: creator/role/source, declared cardinality, no ordinals, IsDeleted distrust, split/merge policies
items.remedy: Keep.

items.title: Interaction-derived per-feature ΔH/ΔS/volume contracts; the 'silently wrong but valid' compound-tool finding
items.claim: Interaction-derived per-feature ΔH/ΔS/volume contracts; the 'silently wrong but valid' compound-tool finding
items.remedy: Keep.

items.title: Epistemic honesty: confirmed/corrected/unverified labels, negative findings recorded, gaps documented
items.claim: Epistemic honesty: confirmed/corrected/unverified labels, negative findings recorded, gaps documented
items.evidence: reports/DSL mathematical foundations.md; spikes RESULTS; NOTES
items.remedy: Keep.

items.title: Verifier before model
items.claim: Verifier before model
items.remedy: Keep.

items.title: Direct manipulation edits intent; edited intent marks the solution stale
items.claim: Direct manipulation edits intent; edited intent marks the solution stale
items.remedy: Keep.

items.title: 'Why is this here?' inspector traces each face to feature, intent word and node
items.claim: 'Why is this here?' inspector traces each face to feature, intent word and node

hn_comments.comment: 'Capture design intent, not coordinates' was PTC's sales pitch in 1988. ICAD and NX Knowledge Fusion did rule packs in the 90s. Every KBE shop I've seen ended with a 40,000-line rule base one retiree understood. What's different this time besides YAML?
hn_comments.fairness: Fair. NOV-01/02, PAIN-04. The honest answer (executable checks tied to kernel history; an LLM to absorb the authoring cost) needs evidence the repo doesn't have yet.

hn_comments.comment: I read the whole README looking for the model. There isn't one. It's a build123d/OCP wrapper with asserts and a very long design doc. Nine 'learned skills' in a table, zero training runs.
hn_comments.fairness: Mostly fair (ISS-04); unfair in that the survey argues persuasively for building the verifier first.

hn_comments.comment: The demo bracket shows PASS. Its wall screws sit at 9 and 50 mm up a 150 mm leg because the gusset ate the top. Take moments: ~31 N·m from 20 kg at 160 mm gives ~600 N pull-out on the top screw into drywall anchors, before the safety factor. The 'PASS' is Euler's formula passing. That badge will get someone's shelf on the floor.
hn_comments.fairness: Fair with simplified-model caveat. INC-06, ISS-01, PAIN-05.

hn_comments.comment: Read Bidarra & Bronsvoort 'Semantic feature modelling' (CAD 2000). Read Hoffmann & Kim on valid parameter ranges, and Kripac '97 and Capoyleas/Chen/Hoffmann '96 for naming (you cite those, good). Then the Owen/D-Cubed root-identification papers. Your 'stability harness' samples 9 points of a space people have computed exact validity intervals for.

Ignore the grand vision. cardinality=exactly(2), never trusting IsDeleted, ΔH asserts per feature, and 'overlapping compound tool silently cuts nothing' are worth the visit. The spike RESULTS files are the most honest OCCT write-up I've read. Please ship the reference layer as a standalone library.

I don't know my intent until I've drawn forty thumbnails and hated thirty-eight of them. This automates the last 20% of my job, the part I already do fine in SolidWorks, and makes me write a requirements doc for the fun part.
hn_comments.fairness: Fair for early ID, less so for configurators. PAIN-01, PAIN-12.

hn_comments.comment: Tarski, Cartan–Dieudonné, Laman, Euler–Poincaré, r-sets, projective geometric algebra… for an L-bracket with four holes. Mathematical cosplay.
hn_comments.fairness: Half fair: the report is careful and self-labelled, but the docs carry more theory than the code uses (MATH-05) and the Euler check is parity (MATH-01).

hn_comments.comment: FeatureScript already has qCreatedBy, custom features written the same way as built-ins, tracking queries and attributes. The authors know this because they cite it. Why build a new kernel stack and GUI instead of an Onshape tab plus FeatureScript, where the users and Parasolid already are?
hn_comments.fairness: Fair strategic question. PAIN-09, docs/user-experience.md §5; standalone is defensible for determinism and running locally, but the round trip decides adoption in organisations.
